data.title: Cerri, Boskovich & Allard, LLP File Lawsuit Against Cabrillo Unified School District Alleging Years of Sexual Abuse by Former Teacher and Coach
data.description:
Cerri, Boskovich & Allard, LLP File Lawsuit Against Cabrillo Unified School District Alleging Years of Sexual Abuse by Former Teacher and Coach

A civil lawsuit filed by the law firm of Cerri, Boskovich & Allard, LLP in San Mateo County Superior Court alleges that Cabrillo Unified School District (CUSD) failed to protect a student from years of sexual abuse by former teacher and coach Paul Farnsworth, known as “Farnz”, despite repeated warning signs and alleged violations of appropriate adult-student boundaries.

The lawsuit, brought on behalf of a plaintiff identified as Jane Doe, alleges that Farnsworth began grooming her when she was a seventh-grader at Manuel F. Cunha Intermediate School in 2004. According to the complaint, the alleged grooming escalated into ongoing sexual abuse that continued throughout her high school years at Half Moon Bay High School through 2010 and into adulthood.

The complaint describes an alleged pattern of boundary violations, including Farnsworth singling out female students, driving minors in his personal vehicle, taking Doe to meals alone, sharing personal information with students, asking them to babysit, and making sexualized comments. 

The lawsuit further alleges that Farnsworth repeatedly invited Doe to his classroom at El Granada Elementary School after hours, locked the doors, and blacked out or covered the windows. The complaint also describes alleged incidents in which Farnsworth transported Doe in his personal vehicle and shared hotel rooms with her during school-sponsored athletic travel.

According to the filing, Farnsworth frequently hugged Doe and displayed physical affection toward her at school-sponsored cross-country and track meets, sometimes within direct view of other high school coaches.

The lawsuit alleges that district employees and administrators witnessed Farnsworth spending unusual amounts of time alone with Doe and engaging in physical displays of affection but failed to report, investigate, or address his conduct. It contends that CUSD did not take appropriate steps to intervene, increase supervision, or discipline or terminate Farnsworth, allowing the alleged abuse to continue for six years.

The lawsuit follows Farnsworth’s August 13, 2026 arrest and October 13, 2026 no contest plea to a felony lewd act charge involving a 14- or 15-year-old child. He admitted to taking advantage of his position of trust and confidence as Doe’s coach and that she was particularly vulnerable. According to the complaint, he remained employed by CUSD until his arrest.

“School districts are legally obligated to maintain safe environments for children entrusted to their care,” said Lauren Cerri, attorney at Cerri, Boskovich & Allard. “For years, Paul Farnsworth’s boundary violations were visible and continuous, parents and students knew something was not right, yet administrators and staff looked the other way while a student in their custody was repeatedly harmed. This lawsuit seeks full accountability for the institutional failures that allowed this to occur in plain view, as well as justice for the lasting trauma inflicted on our client.”

data.title: Brayton Purcell LLP Welcomes Federal Bill Addressing Artificial Stone Silicosis Epidemic
data.description:
Brayton Purcell LLP Welcomes Federal Bill Addressing Artificial Stone Silicosis Epidemic

Brayton Purcell LLP Welcomes Federal Bill Addressing Artificial Stone Silicosis Epidemic

PR Newswire

NOVATO, Calif., Oct. 16, 2026

Silicosis Prevention and Treatment Act would expand screening, treatment, education, and patient care as California artificial stone fabrication workers face a growing number of cases

NOVATO, Calif., Oct. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Brayton Purcell LLP welcomes new federal legislation that would expand medical care and resources for workers affected by artificial stone silicosis, a preventable, progressive, incurable, and fatal occupational lung disease affecting countertop fabrication workers in California and across the United States.

U.S. Representatives Lou Correa of California and Maxine Dexter, M.D., of Oregon introduced the Silicosis Prevention and Treatment Act on October 14, 2026. The legislation would establish a federal grant program to support screening, diagnosis, treatment, education, pulmonary rehabilitation, and coordinated patient care.

The legislation is especially important in California, where more than 662 confirmed silicosis cases have been reported. More than 135 are in Orange County. Rep. Correa's district includes Anaheim's "Tile Mile," where many workers cut and fabricate artificial stone slabs into custom countertops.

In announcing the bill, Rep. Correa directly addressed the artificial stone fabrication workers in his district:

"No worker should lose their ability to breathe because of the job they do to support their family. In Anaheim's Tile Mile, workers who cut manufactured stone countertops are being diagnosed with silicosis at alarming rates. Silicosis is preventable, and early detection can save lives. This bill puts resources into the hands of the clinics and hospitals that treat these workers, so they get the care they need before it's too late."

Artificial Stone Silicosis in California

Artificial stone, also referred to as engineered stone or manufactured stone, is at least 90% respirable crystalline silica. The remaining approximately 10% consists of highly toxic dyes, resins, glues, and heavy metals.

Cutting, grinding, and polishing artificial stone creates nano-sized, high-surface-area respirable crystalline silica dust. During fabrication, the highly toxic dyes, resins, glues, and heavy metals that make up approximately 10% of artificial stone release volatile organic compounds (VOCs).

Artificial stone workers inhale the nano-sized, high-surface-area respirable crystalline silica dust created during fabrication. These particles become lodged deeply in the lungs, causing inflammation and permanent scarring. Respiratory function progressively declines, leading to 24/7 supplemental oxygen dependence and, in severe cases, the need for double lung transplantation. Artificial stone silicosis is preventable, progressive, incurable, and fatal. There is no cure.

California's confirmed cases, and the concentration of cases in Orange County, underscore the importance of medical resources for workers diagnosed with artificial stone silicosis.

Bill Would Expand Resources for Affected Workers

The Silicosis Prevention and Treatment Act would establish a competitive grant program administered through the Health Resources and Services Administration and authorize $10 million annually for fiscal years 2027 through 2031.

Eligible recipients would include federally qualified health centers, hospitals, state and local health departments, and nonprofit healthcare clinics and providers.

Grant funding could support:

  • Outreach and education;
  • Screening, diagnosis, and treatment;
  • Education for patients, families, and affected workers;
  • Counseling related to state and federal compensation programs;
  • Individual patient care plans, referrals, and care coordination; and
  • Pulmonary rehabilitation.

Grant recipients would provide treatment to people with silicosis regardless of their ability to pay.

While the federal program would operate nationwide, the legislation has particular significance for California's artificial stone fabrication workers who are already confronting the disease.

Rep. Dexter, a pulmonologist, said:

"A paycheck should never come at the cost of your ability to breathe. As a pulmonologist, I know the devastating impacts of lung disease. As cases rapidly increase, it is critical that we are educating those that are most at risk for this irreversible disease. The Silicosis Prevention and Treatment Act will create funding for healthcare facilities to disseminate information and raise awareness about this progressive lung disease. We must protect the people whose hard work builds our communities."

Read the full proposed Silicosis Prevention and Treatment Act:
https://correa.house.gov/imo/media/doc/silicosis_prevention_and_treatment_act.pdf

Brayton Purcell Welcomes Increased Attention to Artificial Stone Silicosis

Brayton Purcell LLP represents artificial stone workers and families affected by silicosis and welcomes the increased federal attention to the disease and the medical needs of workers already diagnosed.

James Nevin of Brayton Purcell LLP said:

"For people living with artificial stone silicosis, access to knowledgeable medical care, screening, pulmonary rehabilitation, and other support can be critically important. This bill recognizes the serious medical needs facing these patients and proposes meaningful resources to help address them. We welcome the increased attention to this devastating and irreversible disease that has affected artificial stone workers and their families."

For California artificial stone countertop workers, the proposed legislation represents an important effort to direct additional resources toward screening, diagnosis, treatment, pulmonary rehabilitation, education, and coordinated care.

Brayton Purcell LLP and Artificial Stone Silicosis Litigation

Brayton Purcell LLP is an experienced law firm representing workers and families affected by artificial stone silicosis.

Individuals diagnosed with artificial stone silicosis may have legal rights related to the artificial stone products involved in their exposure. Those rights depend on the circumstances of each case, including the products involved, exposure history, medical history, and applicable law.

About Brayton Purcell LLP

Brayton Purcell LLP represents individuals and families in complex litigation involving occupational disease and toxic exposures. The firm's attorneys have decades of experience advocating for people and families affected by serious diseases associated with hazardous products and substances.

PASCAGOULA, Miss., Oct. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- HII’s (NYSE:HII) Ingalls Shipbuilding division will host an on-site hiring event from 8 a.m. to noon, Saturday, October 24 at the Ingalls Maritime Training Academy, 2721 Jerry St. Pé Highway, Pascagoula. The event is open to skilled, semi-skilled and entry-level applicants. Pre-registration is recommended and attendees should bring two forms of valid ID.

As the nation’s premier builder of Navy surface combatants and amphibious ships, Ingalls relies on a highly skilled workforce to deliver ships that support national security. The upcoming hiring event will give job seekers an opportunity to learn more about Ingalls’ mission, long-term career pathways and training opportunities. Veterans and transitioning service members are encouraged to attend the event to explore careers where military experience directly translates into mission-driven work.

“Every ship built by the hardworking men and women here at Ingalls contributes directly to America’s security,” said Susan Jacobs, Ingalls Shipbuilding vice president of human resources and administration. “We’re looking to hire people who want to be a part of that mission and who want stable, well-paying jobs that make a difference.”


A photo accompanying this release is available at: https://www.hii.com/newsroom.

Ingalls offers long-term career stability, competitive wages and comprehensive benefits supported by a strong pipeline of future work. The company provides weekly pay, market-driven wage increases for skilled trades, holiday pay, comprehensive medical plan options, financial wellness resources, and clear pathways for professional growth that stand out among employers across the region.

Ingalls is hiring for select positions, including:

  • Electricians

data.title: Paris Hilton Unites 200+ Neurodivergent Creators for UNSTOPPABLE, a First-of-Its-Kind ADHD Creator Summit
data.description:
Paris Hilton Unites 200+ Neurodivergent Creators for UNSTOPPABLE, a First-of-Its-Kind ADHD Creator Summit

The immersive summit convened leading creators with a combined audience reach of over 500 million, alongside experts and advocates, to celebrate neurodiversity and change the conversation around ADHD

PHOTO AND VIDEO ASSETS HERE AND HERE

Paris Hilton, through her nonprofit 11:11 Media Impact and presented by Loop Earplugs, brought together more than 200 neurodivergent creators with a combined audience reach of 500 million+, along with advocates and experts, for UNSTOPPABLE, a first-of-its-kind ADHD creator summit held at Slivington Manor in Los Angeles on October 15. The daylong event featured interactive activations, educational sessions, and candid conversations designed to build community and equip creators with tools to help their audiences better understand ADHD.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261016756187/en/

Paris Hilton Photo: Ashley Osborne

Hosted during ADHD Awareness Month, UNSTOPPABLE grew out of Hilton’s advocacy for the neurodivergent community after she began speaking openly about growing up with undiagnosed ADHD. The goal was to challenge misconceptions, share lived experiences, and explore how greater awareness and understanding can help people embrace and celebrate the ways their minds work.

Recognizing the powerful role creators play in shaping culture, Hilton designed a gathering to educate the creators about their mind so they could then share credible, expert-backed information with their audiences, and then give them the space to connect and play through the Festival portion of the event.

Creators in attendance included Lizzo, Haley Baylee, Rebecca Zamolo, ​​Dr. Sasha Hamdani, Whitney Cummings, Miranda Cosgrove, Elyse Myers, Tanner Smith, Alex Partridge, Nik Hobrecker, Thea Donaldson, Armani White, CJ Perry, Chloe Hayden, and Vas J Morgan, among others.

“Bringing UNSTOPPABLE to life has been so special to me. Seeing this community come together, sharing stories, connecting with each other, and celebrating the unique way our minds work is exactly what I hoped today would be. I know what it feels like to grow up feeling misunderstood, and I wanted to create a space where people feel seen, supported, and celebrated for who they are. These creators have the power to take what we shared today to millions of people. If even one person watching their stories feels less alone, more understood, or finally sees their ADHD as something they don’t have to hide, then today has made a difference. And this is just the beginning.”

An Experience Built Around the ADHD Mind

Moving beyond the traditional conference format, UNSTOPPABLE offered an immersive environment designed around how neurodivergent people experience the world. Participants explored interactive, sensory, creative, and regulation-based activations designed to encourage movement, connection, self-expression, and calm, while engaging with experts and fellow creators throughout the day.

The educational program brought together leading voices in neuroscience, mental health, and neurodiversity from Understood.org, Jake Collective, The Mental Health Coalition, The Jed Foundation, and Creators 4 Mental Health. Conversations focused on the science behind ADHD, the importance of combatting misinformation, and how creators can share personal stories responsibly while connecting their audiences with credible resources.

The day culminated in a fireside conversation featuring Hilton, Anton Rabie, Co-Founder and Chair of Spin Master® and author of the upcoming book Different: An Unconventional Guide to Becoming Your Best Self, and Stacey Bendet, Founder and CEO of Alice + Olivia, moderated by Nancy Armstrong, Certified ADHD Parenting Coach and creator of the award-winning documentary The Disruptors.

The conversation explored the importance of embracing neurodiversity, challenging childhood misconceptions about ADHD, and finding confidence in the ways people’s minds work differently. The discussion also touched on the role of supportive environments, the power of self-acceptance, and how perceived challenges can become strengths in leadership, creativity and building a career.

  • Anton Rabie on helping children build confidence: “I think the first thing parents need to do is double down on investing the time to identify what makes your kid different. Then find the environment and immerse them in that environment so that they feel the wins. And you build their confidence, and you build their self-esteem.”
  • Stacey Bendet on childhood struggles and finding her own path to success: “I remember my mom reading me my first-grade report card, and it said, ‘We are so proud of Stacey for becoming more tolerant of others this year.’ But now I lead a team of over 400 people, so you can make it despite your childhood struggles.”

Turning Awareness Into Action

UNSTOPPABLE was designed to extend beyond a single day. The summit also serves as the foundation for a forthcoming public service announcement, produced in partnership with The Mental Health Coalition, featuring intimate portraits of participating creators and celebrities sharing candid reflections on how ADHD has shaped their lives.

  • “When creators share their ADHD stories, it can help start conversations that may not otherwise happen. And pairing that storytelling with expert-backed information can turn awareness into real support,” said Sarah Greenberg, psychotherapist and vice president of expertise and behavioral health innovation at Understood.org. “At UNSTOPPABLE, leading mental health and neurodivergence experts gave creators facts and trusted resources to better understand their brains, share their stories with confidence, and help their audiences find accurate ADHD information to help them thrive.”
  • “At Loop, we believe unwanted noise should never stand in the way of enjoying a social event, finding deep focus or waking fully refreshed. Our brand ethos is to empower people to live life fully and experience the world on their own terms. We’re proud that Loop can be one of the tools people choose to help them embrace their strengths and feel truly unstoppable,” said Dimitri O, Co-founder, Loop Earplugs.

Presented by Loop Earplugs, the summit also reflected the partnership between Hilton and the brand, which grew from Hilton’s personal use of Loop earplugs and her collaboration with the company on a limited-edition Loop Engage™. Throughout October, in recognition of ADHD Awareness Month, Loop is donating a portion of proceeds from every Loop Engage purchase to 11:11 Media Impact, with a guaranteed minimum contribution of $150,000. This support will help fund 11:11 Media Impact’s neurodivergent-focused programming, education in partnership with Understood.org, content aimed at reducing the stigma around ADHD, and initiatives supporting early diagnosis within the neurodivergent community. Additional UNSTOPPABLE partners include Hilton Hotels, United Talent Agency, and Kinetic Sand®.

About 11:11 Media Impact

11:11 Media Impact is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit founded by Paris Hilton to turn lived experience into lasting change. Through strategic advocacy, impact storytelling, and philanthropic investment, the organization works across three priority areas: ending institutional child abuse in the Troubled Teen Industry, advancing inclusion for neurodivergent people, and protecting women and girls from nonconsensual intimate imagery, including AI-generated deepfakes. Since its founding, 11:11 Media Impact has helped secure passage of the federal Stop Institutional Child Abuse Act and 20 state laws strengthening protections for youth in congregate care, alongside federal and state action against nonconsensual explicit deepfakes. Through ADHD awareness campaigns, creator convenings, and original storytelling, the organization is building a movement that celebrates neurodivergent minds. 11:11 Media Impact also supports LGBTQIA+ direct service organizations and crisis response efforts.

Media Contact
Natalie Yallouz
Buzzer PR for 11:11 Media
natalie@buzzerpr.com

data.title: BROAD ARROW DELIVERS SPECTACULAR FERRARIS ACROSS GLOBAL MARKETS AS SUPERCAR AND HYPERCAR DEMAND CLIMBS

Grosse Pointe, Michigan, Oct. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Broad Arrow Auctions and Private Sales, driven by Hagerty (NYSE: HGTY), is at the forefront of the modern Ferrari collector market as it continues to show significant growth in 2026. Analysis from Hagerty shows a surge in demand for modern supercars which now account for 38 percent of the global collector car auction market. Hypercars have seen a similar increase, representing 32 percent of the auction market, with both segments being driven in large part by the demand for highly desirable Ferrari models.

Broad Arrow Auctions has released another highly desirable lineup of Ferrari hypercars and supercars for its upcoming second annual Las Vegas Auction, set for October 31 in partnership with Concours at Wynn Las Vegas.

Latest highlights are led by a 2025 Ferrari Daytona SP3 (Estimate: $16,000,000 - $18,000,000), chassis number 314846, finished in the exquisite Tailor Made shade of Verde Francesca over a two-tone Nero Alcantara and Mustard Aunde Jeans interior. Offered from its original owner, the curator of an exceptional private collection, the SP3 is one of just 600 examples produced and displays just 81 miles at cataloging. The second model in Ferrari’s sought after “Icona” series, the Daytona SP3 is many things—a rolling tribute to one of the marque’s most triumphant afternoons, a showcase of naturally aspirated engineering at its peak, and quite possibly the final chapter in a mid-engine, naturally aspirated lineage that began nearly sixty years ago. The car on offer is equipped with numerous carbon fiber elements, airbrushed fender shield, a suspension lifter, and a full complement of factory accessories.

“The collector car market has quickly recognized the significance of the Daytona SP3 in Ferrari’s history,” says Barney Ruprecht, Vice President of Auctions for Broad Arrow. “In the few short years since the SP3's reveal, values have climbed sharply, reflecting both the model's extreme exclusivity, and a growing understanding that it may represent the final expression Ferrari’s naturally aspirated V12 for the road. This is a particularly special example of the 600 made, with a bespoke specification that’s sure to appeal to today’s most discerning collectors.”

Additional thrilling Ferrari highlights coming to Broad Arrow Las Vegas Auction include:

2014 Ferrari LaFerrari (Estimate: $8,500,000 - $10,000,000)

This is a low-mileage, extensively specified example of the first hybrid hypercar from Maranello, producing a combined 950 horsepower from its 6.3-liter V12 hybrid powerplant. One of approximately 120 examples delivered new to the US, the LaFerrari on offer is finished in iconic Rosso Corsa over Nero leather with Rosso accents, recently serviced, and accompanied by its battery charger, fitted car cover, and tool kit. It is offered with a two-year Certified Pre-Owned warranty, including coverage of its hybrid battery, valid through October 2028.

2003 Ferrari Enzo (Estimate: $6,500,000 - $8,500,000)

One of only 111 delivered new to the US market, this true driver’s example of Ferrari’s singular turn-of-the-century hypercar shows under 18,000 miles at cataloging. It has been refinished by Carrozzeria Zanasi in Maranello to its original Rosso Corsa and features a Pelle Nera interior. Classiche certified and serviced in 2026 by Ferrari Dallas at a cost exceeding $10,000, this is an eminently usable example of the iconic hypercar that carries the legacy of Enzo Ferrari, prepared to be enjoyed the way its namesake intended.

2011 Ferrari 599 SA Aperta (Estimate: $4,100,000 - $4,500,000)

This exceptionally rare supercar is one of only 80 special series SA Aperta models produced in celebration of Pininfarina’s 80th anniversary. Finished in classic Rosso Corsa over Nero leather with Rosso details, it is offered in near-new condition with just 745 miles, $87,000 in optional extras, and an exhilarating zero-to-62 miles per hour time of 3.6 seconds with a top speed of 202 miles per hour.

Additional modern collectible Ferraris on offer include the just-announced 106-mile time capsule 1997 Ferrari F50, a 2015 Ferrari 458 Speciale A offered without reserve, a 2015 Ferrari 458 Speciale, a 2001 Ferrari 550 Barchetta Pininfarina, and more. View the more than 25 Ferraris on offer in the Las Vegas Auction here.

Following the fantastic results for many Ferrari supercars at Broad Arrow recent Zoute Concours Auction, the company continues its momentum in Europe with its second annual Zürich Auction on November 7, the official auction partner of the renowned Auto Zürich show. Exceptional Ferraris are set for the sale at the Dolder Grand hotel, including two of the market’s most desirable models, offered without reserve.

2015 Ferrari LaFerrari (Estimate: CHF 5'500'000 - CHF 7'500'000 | Offered Without Reserve)

Striking in Bianco Fuji over a Bianchi/Neri leather interior, the LaFerrari on offer in Zürich is one of approximately 50 examples specified with the exposed carbon-fiber roof. This delivery-mileage example is offered with the common “sticky buttons” issue remedied and with a new high-voltage battery. The LaFerrari is a well-cared-for example of an essential acquisition—one of the most significant Ferraris ever built.

2017 Ferrari F12tdf (Estimate: CHF 1'300'000 - CHF 1'500'000 | Offered Without Reserve)

The F12tdf was the last Ferrari model to be styled in collaboration with Pininfarina and features a 6.3-litre V12, the most powerful naturally aspirated V12 when it was introduced. This particular car was delivered new to Switzerland finished in distinctive special-order matte Alluminio Opaco over Nero Alcantara with matter carbon fiber and Giallo accents throughout. Offered with just two owners and 13,601 kilometers from new, this is a recently serviced, compelling example of a highly coveted Ferrari.

View the more than 13 Ferraris on offer in Broad Arrow’s Zürich Auction here.

Broad Arrow Private Sales has connected the buyers and sellers of many of the most in-demand Ferrari supercars in recent months, with successful sales throughout its international network. data.title: Egan-Jones Examines AI's Pressure on Firms That Sell Expertise by the Hour
data.description:
Egan-Jones Examines AI's Pressure on Firms That Sell Expertise by the Hour

Egan-Jones Examines AI's Pressure on Firms That Sell Expertise by the Hour

PR Newswire

NEW YORK, Oct. 16, 2026

NEW YORK, Oct. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Egan-Jones released a commentary examining how advances in artificial intelligence could compress margins at firms that sell expertise by the hour, with ripple effects for venture capital returns and the US housing market. Egan-Jones regards broad economic disruption as a near certainty now that the latest models have crossed a threshold of quality and speed for widespread adoption.

Audit, consulting, law and engineering firms sit at the center of the analysis. They sell intellectual capital by the hour, and Egan-Jones expects their prices to decline significantly as small teams using AI match the output of large practices. KPMG pressed its auditor to pass on AI savings and won a 14% fee cut, a demand the commentary expects every audit client to make.

Seniority offers little protection. Senior staff sell expertise that AI now makes readily available, and their leverage buys time but not a guarantee of future employment. Lower barriers to entry let new rivals compete on price and quality without years of hiring.

For software providers, the commentary cites the Model Context Protocol, an open standard that lets AI models connect directly to outside software and data, as making a product's own interface matter less. It sees pricing power eroding for legacy software and data providers, where a single product launch can now reprice a company in a day.

For private markets, Egan-Jones describes a quiet deflation in the value of money. Startups reach scale faster and, on less capital, because AI does much of the work venture funding once paid for, compressing venture returns. Few limited partners, it suggests, have priced this in.

Job losses among screen-based workers are the channel to watch for housing. Home prices rose 1.6% in the year to June, below inflation of 3.5%, and the median new home cost 4.7 times median household income in 2025, up from 3.6 times in 1984. Egan-Jones' view is short-term downward pressure on prices, while the long-run case for urban land holds.

The commentary was not written by Egan-Jones' credit analysts. It offers institutional investors and risk managers a framework for assessing the structural pressures building across professional services, private markets and housing.

data.title: DHL Group Lifts Guidance After Positive Earnings, Strong Peak-Season Forecast
data.description:
By Andrea Figueras 




  DHL Group upgraded its outlook for 2026 on the back of positive momentum and prospects of a strong seasonal peak in the last quarter of the year. 



  The German logistics company said Friday that it now expects earnings before interest and taxes to surpass 7 billion euros, or $7.86 billion, compared with a prior forecast of more than 6.5 billion euros. The group intends to review its midterm earnings guidance in March. 



  "Business development in the third quarter showed a broad-based growth in demand and, overall, positive earnings momentum for the group, particularly in the DHL Express division," it said. 



  According to preliminary figures, the group made EBIT of roughly 1.71 billion euros for the quarter through September, up around 16% compared with the same period a year earlier. Group revenue jumped more than 12% on year to nearly 22.6 billion euros. 



  The company also upgraded its target for free cash flow excluding net mergers and acquisitions to more than 3.2 billion euros, up from approximately 3 billion euros previously. 



  Capital expenditure is now estimated at around 3.6 billion euros from a prior range between 3 billion euros and 3.3 billion euros. 



  DHL plans to publish its third-quarter report on Nov. 5. 





  Write to Andrea Figueras at andrea.figueras@wsj.com
